recent_answers.question: Has the government identified hospitals in high-risk haze areas and proactively placed suitable specialists, especially lung specialists, there?

recent_answers.question: Should schools close and outdoor activities be restricted at certain IPU levels, and does KKM give advice on this?
recent_answers.answer: KKM advises limiting outdoor activities above IPU 100 and advises closing schools, kindergartens and nurseries above IPU 200; closure decisions rest with the KPM and KPT ministers under the National Haze Action Plan.

recent_answers.question: What actions and initiatives does the ministry take to address the public health impact of haze, including cooperation with JAS and agencies?
recent_answers.answer: The ministry runs year-round haze-related illness surveillance at 78 sentinel facilities, reports rising URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis cases, adds medical supplies, and cooperates with JAS, METMalaysia, NADMA, KPM and KBS, and advises the public to monitor IPU.

debate.summary_en: After being called by Deputy Speaker Puan Alice Lau Kiong Yieng, Tuan Cha Kee Chin (Rasah) asked the Works Minister for the current status, progress percentage, expected completion date and causes of delay for the FT362 upgrade from Simpang Tol Bandar Ainsdale to Seremban town. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan, Deputy Minister of Works, replied that completion is scheduled for 17 May 2029, progress is 7.62 per cent against a scheduled 7.62 per cent, and land acquisition for 18 of 46 private lots remains, expected to finish by the end of November 2026. Tuan Cha Kee Chin then asked for the results and preliminary findings of the Jalan Sungai Ujong traffic study, including the two-week closure of a traffic light junction after the Seremban toll plaza exit, whether it would be fully implemented, and when results would be announced. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan replied that the junction is 155 metres from the PLUS junction against a 300-metre guideline, that the closure eased traffic but the U-turn at Jalan Labu FT362 is small and narrow so a long-term upgrade is proposed, and that congestion persisted because road users made unauthorised U-turns at Palm Mall, so JKR could not yet reach a conclusive finding, and he referred the Rasah MP to JKR Seremban. Dato’ Sri Dr. Haji Ismail bin Abd Muttalib (Maran) asked how many contractors had been penalised, including contract termination, what losses the government had incurred, and the status of the FT83 Jengka 8 to Pusat Jengka upgrade. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan replied that 70 to 75 per cent of the troubled projects among about 850 are caused by contractors, that the loss has not yet been assessed, and that the FT83 question will be answered in writing, while Tuan Zakri bin Hassan (Kangar) stood to ask question 11 with no substantive content.
debate.summary_ms: Selepas dijemput oleh Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Puan Alice Lau Kiong Yieng, Tuan Cha Kee Chin (Rasah) meminta Menteri Kerja Raya menyatakan status terkini, peratus kemajuan, tarikh dijangka siap dan punca kelewatan bagi projek menaik taraf Jalan FT362 dari Simpang Tol Bandar Ainsdale ke bandar Seremban. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan, Timbalan Menteri Kerja Raya, menjawab bahawa projek dijadual siap pada 17 Mei 2029, kemajuan ialah 7.62 peratus berbanding jadual 7.62 peratus, dan pengambilan balik tanah bagi 18 daripada 46 lot persendirian masih berbaki, dijangka selesai pada penghujung November 2026. Tuan Cha Kee Chin kemudian bertanya tentang status dan dapatan awal kajian penyuraian trafik di Jalan Sungai Ujong, termasuk penutupan simpang lampu isyarat selama dua minggu selepas exit Plaza Tol Seremban, sama ada ia akan dilaksanakan sepenuhnya, dan bila keputusan akan diumumkan. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan menjawab bahawa persimpangan itu berjarak 155 meter dari persimpangan PLUS berbanding garis panduan 300 meter, penutupan itu melancarkan trafik tetapi U-turn di Jalan Labu FT362 kecil dan sempit sehingga naik taraf jangka panjang dicadangkan, dan kesesakan berterusan kerana pengguna jalan raya membuat U-turn tidak sah di Palm Mall, justeru JKR belum dapat membuat kesimpulan konklusif; beliau merujuk Ahli Parlimen Rasah kepada JKR Seremban. Dato’ Sri Dr. Haji Ismail bin Abd Muttalib (Maran) bertanya berapa ramai kontraktor telah dikenakan tindakan termasuk penamatan kontrak, berapa kerugian kerajaan, dan status menaik taraf Jalan Persekutuan FT83 Jengka 8 ke Pusat Jengka. Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan menjawab bahawa 70 hingga 75 peratus projek sakit daripada kira-kira 850 projek disebabkan kontraktor, kerugian belum ditaksir, dan soalan FT83 akan dijawab secara bertulis, manakala Tuan Zakri bin Hassan (Kangar) bangun untuk soalan 11 tanpa kandungan substantif.

speech_rows.label: Timbalan Menteri Kerja Raya [Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan]
speech_rows.name: Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan
speech_rows.text:
Puan Yang di-Pertua, pertanyaan yang dikemukakan oleh Yang Berhormat
Rasah adalah merujuk kepada projek menaik taraf Jalan FT362 dari Seksyen 0.4 ke
Seksyen 3.1, Lingkaran Tengah Seremban dan membina jejambat merentasi
Lebuhraya Utara Selatan, daerah Seremban, Negeri Sembilan.
Projek ini telah diluluskan di dalam Rolling Plan 3, Rancangan Malaysia
Kedua Belas. Skop projek ini ialah menaik taraf jalan tunggal dua lorong kepada jalan
kembar empat lorong dua hala sepanjang 2.7 kilometer termasuk membina jambatan
dengan piawaian JKR U5, menaik taraf persimpangan sedia ada, pemasangan lampu
jalan dan lampu isyarat, menaik taraf sistem perparitan, kerja-kerja geoteknik, kerja-
kerja pavement, pemasangan perabot jalan, pengambilan balik tanah dan pengalihan
utiliti.
Surat setuju terima (SST) telah dikeluarkan pada 28 Januari 2025, manakala
tarikh mula tapak adalah pada 9 April 2025. Projek ini dijadual dapat disiapkan pada
17 Mei 2029. Status kemajuan projek sehingga 30 September 2026 telah mencapai
7.62 peratus berbanding jadual juga sebanyak 7.62 peratus, iaitu 100 peratus ikut
jadual.
Untuk makluman Ahli Yang Berhormat, proses pengambilan balik tanah PBT
masih belum selesai dengan berbaki 18 lot daripada 46 lot persendirian yang terlibat
di sepanjang jajaran ini. Senarai keutamaan telah diselesaikan PBT dikemukakan
kepada Jabatan Ketua Pengarah Tanah dan Galian Persekutuan (JKPTG).
Keseluruhan proses pengambilan balik tanah ini dijangka dapat diselesaikan
sepenuhnya pada penghujung November 2026.
Pada masa ini, pihak kontraktor sedang melaksanakan kerja-kerja di tapak
yang melibatkan sebahagian lot yang telah selesai pelaksanaan proses pengambilan
balik tanah dan di kawasan tanah kerajaan. Pihak kontraktor juga giat melaksanakan
kerja-kerja fizikal yang melibatkan kerja-kerja pembinaan longkang di tepi jalan di
lokasi tertentu. Penyelarasan bersama syarikat-syarikat utiliti yang terlibat dan agensi
kerajaan yang berkaitan sedang dilaksanakan bagi memastikan isu pengalihan utiliti
dapat diselesaikan dengan segera.
Pihak JKR akan memantau secara rapi bagi memastikan pihak kontraktor
mematuhi spesifikasi yang ditetapkan, kawalan kos dan kualiti keseluruhan projek
selaras dengan Arahan Teknik Jalan yang berkuat kuasa. Kementerian Kerja Raya
melalui JKR selaku agensi pelaksana akan terus memantau kemajuan projek ini
secara berkala bagi memastikan ia dilaksanakan mengikut jadual, berjaya disiapkan
mengikut perancangan.
Sekian, terima kasih.

Projek tersebut akan bersambung ke Jalan Lingkaran Tengah ke bandar
Seremban. Baru-baru ini, JKR Negeri Sembilan telah mengadakan projek penyuraian
trafik di Jalan Sungai Ujong dan penutupan simpang lampu isyarat selepas exit Plaza
Tol Seremban dari arah utara selama dua minggu yang telah dilaksanakan pada 30
September sehingga 13 Oktober, dan mulai 14 Oktober kembali kepada keadaan
asal.
Saya nak tanya kepada pihak Yang Berhormat Timbalan Menteri dan KKR,
apakah status terkini hasil kajian tersebut? Apakah dapatan awal berkenaan dengan
kajian tersebut? Sama ada ia akan dilaksanakan sepenuhnya ikut apa yang berlaku
tempoh hari― dua minggu― ataupun ada pandangan yang berbeza?
Sebab, saya sebagai Ahli Parlimen kawasan tersebut, saya pengguna jalan
raya di situ setiap hari. Sebab, saya rasa ada tempat yang boleh kita tutup tempoh
hari, ada yang kita terlebih tutup. Itu sedikit pandangan saya. Terutamanya simpang
pergi Gateway itu. Kalau untuk JKR Seremban, dia tahu, tak sepatutnya ditutup. Jadi,
saya nak tanya, hasil daripada kajian tersebut, bila akan diumumkan dan apakah
keputusan daripada JKR?
Terima kasih, Puan Yang di-Pertua.

speech_rows.label: Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan
speech_rows.name: Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan
speech_rows.text:
Ya, terima kasih, YB Rasah. Ini
adalah mengenai notis penutupan persimpangan lampu isyarat selepas exit Tol
Seremban yang bermula 30 September dan kita telah tamat melakukannya pada 13
Oktober 2026. Jarak antara persimpangan tol PLUS arah selatan dan persimpangan
Seremban Gateway ini 155 meter. Sepatutnya arahan teknik― garis panduan― dia
perlu 300 meter. Oleh itu, berlakulah apa yang disebut sebagai koordinasi pelepasan
kenderaan yang menjejaskan dan kawalan kelajuan progresif green wave yang
terjejas.
Jadi, penutupan simpang exit tol PLUS telah membolehkan kenderaan
bergerak lancar dari arah Seremban 2, Sendayan menghala ke pusat bandar dan
juga arah pusat bandar ke Seremban 2, Sendayan. Penutupan ini juga telah
menghapuskan kesesakan di tol PLUS kerana tiada lagi kenderaan beratur untuk ke
Seremban 2, Sendayan.
Walau bagaimanapun, kajian dilaksanakan telah mengarahkan trafik untuk
menggunakan U-turn di Jalan Labu FT362 yang turut melibatkan kenderaan panjang,
lebar seperti bas, lori kontena. Dan didapati U-turn ini kecil dan sempit. Maka,
cadangan untuk masa panjang, U-turn ini perlu dinaik taraf.
Sebagai rumusan, apa yang ingin saya sampaikan kepada YB Rasah,
kesesakan masih berlaku di beberapa lokasi Jalan Sungai Ujong sepanjang tempoh
kajian berpunca dari keengganan pengguna jalan raya untuk mematuhi arahan yang
dimaklumkan. Contoh utama adalah apabila pengguna jalan raya enggan
menggunakan U-turn yang dinyatakan, sebaliknya membuat U-turn secara tidak sah
di persimpangan Palm Mall. Tindakan ini telah mengakibatkan kesesakan berlaku
semula dan menyukarkan pihak JKR untuk membuat kesimpulan konklusif atas
keberkesanan kajian.
Untuk maklumat lanjut, YB Rasah bolehlah menemui JKR Seremban
mengenainya. Terima kasih.

speech_rows.name: Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Ahmad bin Haji Maslan
speech_rows.text:
Ya, projek sakit yang ada
daripada lebih kurang 850 projek yang di dalam tangan JKR sekarang ini melibatkan
pelbagai kementerian― kerana kami adalah kementerian pelaksana― 27 lagi adalah

Saya mempengerusikan projek sakit ini sebanyak empat kali dalam masa

Saya akan mempengerusikan satu lagi mesyuarat pada bulan 11 di Sarawak.

qa.question: What is the current status of the FT362 upgrade, including progress percentage, expected completion date and causes of delay?
qa.answer: The project was approved under Rolling Plan 3 of the 12th Malaysia Plan; the letter of acceptance was issued on 28 January 2025 and the site started on 9 April 2025. Completion is scheduled for 17 May 2029 and progress is 7.62 per cent against a scheduled 7.62 per cent, so it is on schedule. 18 of 46 private lots remain for land acquisition, expected to finish by the end of November 2026, and the contractor is working on site while utility relocation is being coordinated.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: The Timbalan Menteri Sumber Manusia, Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim, moved that the bill to amend the Akta Kerja 1955, titled Rang Undang-Undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, be read a second time. M. Kulasegaran (Ipoh Barat) asked which Minister was present, saying the important bill should be brought by the Minister. Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon, the Timbalan Yang di-Pertua, said it was fine and that the Timbalan Menteri could proceed. Kulasegaran said he was very happy the Timbalan Menteri was there and began to ask why, but the extract ends before his question is complete. The Timbalan Yang di-Pertua then told him to continue.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim moved the second and third reading of the Rang Undang-undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, stating that the Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) sets minimum terms for private-sector workers and that the amendments aim to strengthen worker protection and align with ILO standards. He said the bill followed consultations since 2015, was first read on 25 October 2021, and contains 46 clauses: 28 amended, 10 new and six repealed. He outlined several amendments, including extending the written appeal period to the Director General of Labour from 14 to 21 days, extending maternity leave from 60 to 90 days, reducing working hours from 48 to 45 hours a week, and introducing three days of paternity leave for married male workers. His speech ended while he was still describing clause 44 on the presumption of who is an employee and employer.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim, continuing his speech on the Rang Undang-undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, said the bill would insert a new section 101C into Akta 265 on presumptions about who is an employee and employer, remove Bahagian VIII on women working at night and underground under Fasal 10, remove section 60L under Fasal 26 and section 93 under Fasal 42, and remove the wage-limit clauses under Fasal 15, 29 and 35 so the Act would cover all private-sector workers, with the Jadual Pertama amended by an order to be enforced on a date yet to be decided. He also said the Jabatan Tenaga Kerja Semenanjung Malaysia had 580 officers, a ratio of one officer to 24,207 workers, and hoped the number would rise toward the International Labor Organization's suggested 1:20,000 ratio. Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon asked for a seconder, and Timbalan Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi Datuk Muslimin bin Yahaya seconded the motion. The Deputy Speaker then opened the second reading debate, read out a list of 21 speakers and began with Ahmad Fadhli bin Shaari (Pasir Mas), who started his speech. M. Kulasegaran (Ipoh Barat) raised a point of order asking for 15 or 20 minutes instead of five, and Sivarasa Rasiah (Sungai Buloh) said the House's scheduling should be better arranged and that hurried passage of important amendments was improper, to which the Deputy Speaker replied that another bill was to be debated that day and they would proceed first.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Tuan Sivarasa Rasiah (Sungai Buloh) said there are major issues in this Act and that the other Act is less important, and in S3 he said the matter should be reviewed, that important matters should not be rushed, and that Parliament's role seems diminished, so he asked for it to be studied again. Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon, the Timbalan Yang di-Pertua, acknowledged the points and asked Tuan Ahmad Fadhli bin Shaari (Pasir Mas) to continue. Tuan Ahmad Fadhli welcomed the government's measures to protect workers earning not more than RM2,000 a month or doing manual work, and raised paternity leave under section 60FA, suggesting non-consecutive leave and the Flexible Parental Leave Pay idea from Australia. He also asked whether the government would introduce iddah leave for widows, raised the employer notice on sexual harassment, and asked whether women flight attendants at Malaysia Airlines System (MAS) are allowed to wear the tudung. Tuan M. Kulasegaran (Ipoh Barat) was invited to speak and was given a little extra time, but he made no substantive remarks in the extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Tuan M. Kulasegaran [Ipoh Barat] said the bill, which he said was drafted when his side was in government, had been delayed since March 2020 and that the delay had harmed workers. He argued that the Ministry of Human Resources, rather than the Ministry of Home Affairs, should register foreign workers, that the forced labour provisions let the ministry investigate and act, and that cases should go to court with the Attorney General's permission, and he said JPA should increase its staffing, perhaps to 1,000 people. Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon said he would add three minutes to the speaking time. Tuan M. Kulasegaran then asked for paternity leave to be raised from three days to seven and maternity leave from 90 days to 98, questioned why private-sector workers should get less than government staff, and raised gig workers, the RM1,500 minimum wage, possible employer subsidies, e-wages, and enforcement against domestic workers who are not paid. No minister or deputy minister answered in this extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato’ Haji Che Abdullah bin Mat Nawi [Tumpat] asked for passage, and the Timbalan Yang di-Pertua, Dato’ Mohd Rashid Hasnon, told him he would be called later and invited Sivarasa Rasiah [Sungai Buloh] to speak. Sivarasa Rasiah said some amendments to the Akta Kerja were good but that important opportunities had been missed, and he noted the government’s assurance that the First Schedule would be amended by Ministerial power. He raised the issue of contractors supplying labour, asked the government to abolish the practice, and argued that the forced labour provisions covered only two of the eleven features the Minister had cited. He welcomed the increase of maternity leave to 98 days, criticised the 45-hour weekly working limit and urged it be changed to 40 hours, and called for amendments to strengthen trade unions because workers receive 35.7 per cent of GDP. Dato’ Haji Salim Sharif [Jempol] then supported the bill and asked why the ‘cuti penalti’ for private-sector workers is three days when civil servants enjoy seven, and the extract ends mid-speech. No minister or deputy minister answered in this extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Wong Hon Wai (Bukit Bendera) corrected Dato’ Haji Salim Sharif (Jempol), who had referred to 'cuti penalti', saying it should be 'cuti paterniti', and the Deputy Speaker Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon acknowledged this. Salim Sharif then said paternity leave would cover five births regardless of the number of wives, asked that this be reconsidered, welcomed the wage-payment-through-bank proposal but asked whether payment without banks would be allowed for rural workers, and proposed making failure to pay wages a criminal offence. He supported reducing the working week from 48 to 45 hours, noted the 40-hour standard of 1962, and asked how this would affect productivity and whether employers had been consulted. When the Deputy Speaker asked him to conclude, Salim Sharif said gig workers in e-hailing and p-hailing should be recognised as workers and protected under the Act, noting the amendment has no such provision, and he supported the Rang Undang-undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021. Abdul Latiff bin Abdul Rahman (Kuala Krai) also supported the bill, urging 90-day maternity leave for the private sector, citing Kelantan's practice since 2010, and asked what conditions apply for seven days of paternity leave. He further asked what the government is doing to reduce the share of foreign workers and raise citizen employment in unskilled labour, and warned about foreign workers becoming large business owners.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon invited Yang Berhormat Pokok Sena to speak. Dato' Mahfuz bin Haji Omar [Pokok Sena] said his side did not object in general to the Rang Undang-undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021 and urged a new definition of 'pekerja' covering gig economy workers, so that all types of work that benefit a company would be treated as employment. He asked the government for details of the 500,000 job placements recently announced, including the sectors and companies involved, noting that more than 700,000 job seekers remain registered. He asked what steps would encourage local workers to take up jobs, and proposed that persons with disabilities be promoted as icons of local employment. He also raised overlap between KSM and KDN over foreign workers, questioned the FWCMS system and the RM100 charge per approved worker compared with the earlier ePPAx system, which he said was free, and asked the minister to clear up the negative public perception.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Deputy Chairman Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon invited Dato' Dr. Xavier Jayakumar a/l Arulanandam of Kuala Langat to speak on the Rang Undang-Undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021. Dato' Dr. Xavier Jayakumar asked whether the ministry had studied whether the cost of doing business would rise after the Act is passed, and said the Ministry of Human Resources, Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Home Affairs must play a major role. He said forced labour was being pressed on Malaysia by developed countries, asked the government to review this and to raise it with the ambassadors of the United States and the UK, and asked for protective measures for gig economy workers. On e-wages, he raised informal workers without bank accounts and an ageing population, asked how to help them, and thanked the Prime Minister for announcing a RM1,500 minimum wage in May. He said he supported the Bill as a starting point, and the Deputy Chairman then invited the next speaker.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Tuan Haji Ahmad bin Hassan [Papar] raised complaints about teachers separated from their spouses in Sabah and P.175, asked why the Bill does not define discrimination in the new section 69F, and asked why job seekers were not included in section 67F. He welcomed the extension of maternity leave from 60 to 90 days but was concerned about section 37A, proposed raising paternity leave from three days to seven, asked for the reason for repealing section 44A, and called for Akta 1955 to be amended to require annual wage increases. Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon asked him to summarise. Tuan Haji Ahmad bin Hassan [Papar] then asked for the justification for reducing normal working hours from 48 to 45 per week and about section 60K on foreign workers, and said he supported the Bill. Timbalan Yang di-Pertua Dato' Mohd Rashid Hasnon adjourned the sitting until 2.30 petang, and Tuan Yang di-Pertua then invited the Tebrau Member of Parliament to debate; no minister or deputy minister answered any question in this extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: In the second and third reading debate on the Rang Undang-Undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, Tebrau MP Steven Choong Shiau Yoon welcomed the amendments but asked the Minister whether early stakeholder engagement sessions were held before drafting, how many were held, whether they covered all states, how stakeholder views and responses were taken into account, and whether the increase in operating costs and its economic impact were assessed in detail. He asked how the ministry would ensure that the requirement for employers to obtain the Director General's prior approval before hiring a foreign worker would not worsen the existing reliance on undocumented workers (PATI) and increase corruption, and he asked for an action plan and inspections of every employer every two years to check compliance with KWSP and PERKESO requirements and the new provisions. He concluded by saying he supports the bill. The Speaker then invited Kulai MP Puan Teo Nie Ching to speak. She said she was disappointed that the amendments did not address the needs of working mothers who breastfeed, citing figures from the 2006 National Health and Morbidity Survey, and she described breastfeeding provisions in the United States, the Netherlands and the Philippines. She asked the Minister and Deputy Minister to ensure that the rights and interests of breastfeeding mothers are protected. No reply from a minister or deputy minister is recorded in this extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Jelutong (Tuan Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji) raised a point of order under Standing Order 36(12) about a possibly misleading statement by the Pekan MP in debate on the Labour Act amendment bill, noting that Pekan had not explained the matter and that the Chair had allowed time for an explanation. The Chair said he had received the explanation, had given copies to Pekan and Damansara, and would decide after Damansara responded, because the matter involved detailed facts. Jelutong then argued that a Finance Minister answer to a Bagan question contradicted Pekan's statement and asked whether the matter should be referred to the Privileges Committee, and the Chair said the Pekan MP had spoken of principal not being paid while the Finance Minister said interest was paid and principal would fall due in May. Jelutong said he would refer the matter to Damansara. Setiu (Shaharizukirnain bin Abd Kadir) then debated the bill, supporting the extension of maternity leave from 60 to 90 days while asking what measures would stop employers discriminating against women, whether the Act imposes penalties on employers who cut or withhold pay for leave beyond 60 days, and what mechanisms and enforcement would ensure employers display sexual harassment notices under clause 36, and he supported the higher penalty under clause 34 for failing to investigate complaints.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: The Chair (Tuan Yang di-Pertua) invited Puan Nurul Izzah binti Anwar [Permatang Pauh] to speak on the Kerja (Pindaan) Bill 2021. She said a new Act is needed because the amendment does not regulate gig companies that are employers, and that responsibility for PERKESO contributions should lie with employers and companies, not workers alone. She raised minimum wage, saying the RM1,500 figure was announced before the pandemic, average monthly wages fell nine percent from 2020 to 2021, and the review requirement under Akta Majlis Perundingan Gaji Negara 2011 [Akta 732] may have been relevant four years ago. She said the anti-discrimination provision in the Bill is insufficient because it does not clearly define discrimination, and that Malaysia lags well behind Sweden, Japan and Iceland on paid paternity leave, a point she tied to a statement by Yang Berhormat Kulai. The Chair then thanked her and invited the next speaker.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Tuan Ahmad Tarmizi bin Sulaiman [Sik] asked whether the amendment to the Akta Kerja 1955 takes into account flexibility for working from home (BDR) and whether that method will continue into the endemic phase. He asked whether the ministry held engagement sessions with employers, trade unions and NGOs, and why the forced labour definition does not cover the 11 ILO indicators. He raised concerns that domestic workers paid RM600 and the protections offered under the Act remain inadequate, citing a statement from IDWS, and referred to Malaysia's decline to Tier 3 in the Trafficking In Person (TIP) 2021 report by the Jabatan Negara Amerika Syarikat. He welcomed the proposed new section 60FA on three days of paid paternity leave, and [S2] Tuan Yang di-Pertua then invited the Yang Berhormat for Bukit Bendera to speak, with no minister's reply recorded in this extract.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Wong Hon Wai (Bukit Bendera) said the bill still refers to the TPPA although the CPTPP has replaced it, and noted that the Employment Act 1955 was last amended in 2012 and applies only to Peninsular Malaysia under section 1(2). He asked the Minister whether talks with the Sabah and Sarawak state governments and an extension to the Federal Territory of Labuan had taken place, and asked for clarity on the presumption of employee and employer status in new section 101C, citing the UK Uber case. He argued that gig workers such as e-hailing drivers and Foodpanda riders are not protected, noted that maternity leave was raised from 60 to 98 days and paternity leave from five to seven days without extension to gig workers, and asked for legislative guidance on 'discrimination in employment' in section 69F. Chair invited Tumpat to speak. Che Abdullah bin Mat Nawi (Tumpat) said the bill aims to meet international standards, including the TPPA, the Malaysia-US labour consistency plan, protection against discrimination and forced labour, and maternity benefits. He said Muslim women should be allowed by employers to cover their aurat, raised by the Pasir Mas Member, and commented on the Ipoh Barat Member's remark that the amendments were drafted under Pakatan Harapan, saying the issue did not receive the government's attention.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji (Jelutong) asked Dato' Haji Che Abdullah bin Mat Nawi (Tumpat) whether, as a government member, he would ask the Minister to issue a notice to the Indian Ambassador over the ban on hijab-wearing schoolchildren in Karnataka. Dato' Haji Che Abdullah said the right to carry out religious obligations is fundamental and that he agreed to fight for it. The Tuan Yang di-Pertua cautioned that the House should not discuss friendly countries, and Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji said the issue was fundamental. Dato' Haji Che Abdullah then asked Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji whether he would support the right of Muslim women workers in Malaysia to cover their aurat, and spoke on foreign worker recruitment based on sector demand, citing construction shortages and the Pan Borneo Highway project. Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji responded that his party's position was against the ban on hijab in schools, referring to the late Karpal Singh. Mohamed Hanipa bin Maidin (Sepang) debated the Rang Undang-Undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, saying the amendments give the Director General considerable powers, such as under section 60K, and that section 69F can be read to protect workers who wear the tudung.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato’ Haji Che Abdullah bin Mat Nawi [Tumpat] said the Kerajaan Pakatan Harapan viewed the headscarf issue as minor, when it is a matter of the right to carry out religious obligations. Tuan Mohamed Hanipa bin Maidin [Sepang] replied that the Tumpat MP might not fully understand his explanation, then supported protections for pregnant women workers, citing a court case about an MAS flight attendant and the newly inserted section. Tuan Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji [Jelutong] asked why no Indian embassy official had been called by Wisma Putra about schoolchildren reportedly barred from wearing hijab, and what PAS's stance was; Tuan Mohamed Hanipa bin Maidin answered that PAS should be asked and accused it of selective discrimination. The Chair reminded Tuan Mohamed Hanipa bin Maidin that his time was up, Tuan Ahmad Tarmizi bin Sulaiman [Sik] told him to sit down, and the Chair asked him to be brief. Tuan Mohamed Hanipa bin Maidin then said section 81H on sexual harassment notices was a good provision but asked for stronger remedies, and called for protection such as insurance for gig economy workers. Dato’ Ramli bin Dato’ Mohd Nor [Cameron Highlands] then invited Puan Hannah Yeoh [Segambut], who supported the Rang Undang-Undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021, welcoming the extension of maternity leave from 60 to 98 days in clause 12, new section 41A barring termination of pregnant workers, paternity leave raised from three to seven days, and section 81H on sexual harassment notices.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato' Ramli bin Dato' Mohd Nor (Cameron Highlands) invited Dato' Abdullah Sani bin Abdul Hamid (Kapar) to debate the Employment (Amendment) Bill 2021 at its second and third reading. Dato' Abdullah Sani said the amendments to the Employment Act 1955 were meant to comply with standards under the Trans-Pacific Partnership Agreement (TPPA), and he cited a raise in the threshold from RM2,000 to RM5,000, a cut in working hours under section 60 from 48 to 45 hours, and maternity leave increased from 60 to 90 days. He said three days of paternity leave was not enough and suggested seven, and he said only eight per cent of workers were unionised and called for protection against union busting and clearer rules on subcontract labour. Datuk Seri Haji Shamsul Iskandar @ Yusre bin Haji Mohd Akin (Hang Tuah Jaya) asked whether stricter laws were needed to protect workers through unions and asked for Dato' Abdullah Sani's view. Dato' Abdullah Sani replied that wider protection against union busting was needed and asked the Minister to explain, and the Chair then invited the Klang MP to speak.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Charles Anthony Santiago [Klang] said that the 2030 target of a 48 per cent labour income share, up from 35 per cent in 2017, is affected by labour laws he considers pro-employer, and asked the government to review existing laws and regulations to strengthen workers' rights, unions and collective bargaining around living wage rather than minimum wage. He welcomed the increase in maternity leave to 98 days and seven days of paternity leave, and supported new section 101C on the presumption of who is an employer and an employee for e-hailing companies. He said the bill failed to remove the RM2,000 threshold, so workers earning above RM2,000 would not be covered by the amended Employment Act, and asked the government to explain this and to make public the MoU with Bangladesh. Dato' Ramli bin Dato' Mohd Nor [Cameron Highlands] noted that about 20 Members had debated the bill and asked the Deputy Minister to reply for 30 minutes, with written replies for Members not in the Chamber. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim [Timbalan Menteri Sumber Manusia] thanked the Members who took part, listed 20 of them by constituency, and said the ministry values all their views; the extract ends before he responds to the issues raised.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato’ Ramli bin Dato’ Mohd Nor [Cameron Highlands] asked the deputy minister to correct the record, saying the Yang Berhormat Batu Kawan was not involved, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim said he was unclear. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim then withdrew the reference to Batu Kawan and said the paternity leave questions raised by several MPs were discussed with the Ministry of Human Resources in 2021, which agreed to raise the leave from three to seven days, with an amendment paper to be proposed at the Committee stage. He said non-consecutive paternity leave was not suitable for now because it differs from the government practice of consecutive leave, and listed the conditions for eligibility, including a limit of five births regardless of the number of wives. Dato’ Haji Salim Sharif [Jempol] called the five-birth limit discriminatory and asked for it to be reviewed, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim replied that the limit was a starting point and that the number of wives was not restricted. Tuan Karupaiya a/l Mutusami [Padang Serai] asked how many wives a husband could claim for, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim answered that Muslims may have up to four wives while Indian men generally have one, with the act to be reviewed every two years.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim (S1) said the ministry welcomed support for adding Industrial Relations Officers, and that the forced labour clause in the Rang Undang-undang Kerja (Pindaan) 2021 matched four ILO indicators. Tuan M. Kulasegaran (S4) asked what mechanism would implement the forced labour provisions, whether ministry officers could bring cases to court, and whether implementation would follow the bill's passage. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim (S5) replied that other forced labour indicators were already covered by existing Acts and that the ministry would take matters through to prosecution once the Act is passed. Tuan M. Kulasegaran (S7) said Malaysia had been placed in Tier 3 of the United States Trafficking of A Person's Report and asked that the ministry, not the police, handle investigations. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim (S16) said loopholes remained and referred to Akta 446 as a further act with forced labour provisions. Tuan Sivarasa Rasiah (S2, S6, S9, S11, S13, S15, S17) stood, interjected or asked to speak without substantive remarks, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim (S18) asked about his speaking time.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato' Ramli bin Dato' Mohd Nor (Cameron Highlands) said he would consider the matter when the time comes. Sivarasa Rasiah (Sungai Buloh) said the forced labour clause in section 90B names only two elements, restriction of movement and threats and intimidation, whereas the 11 internationally recognised forced labour elements he listed are not in the definition, and asked why they were not included. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim replied that the amendment covers the 11 matters, that other forced labour elements fall under other Acts such as the Immigration Act, the Passport Act, Act 446 and the CYP Act, and that the ministry would address the allegations with the US and the ILO in Geneva. Charles Anthony Santiago (Klang) asked whether an employer who keeps workers' passports or provides poor housing could be charged only under the Passport Act or Act 446 rather than for forced labour, and asked that the 11 ILO pointers be aligned into the amendment. Datuk Haji Awang said passport retention falls under immigration in the Home Ministry, accommodation is among the 11 matters, and the ministry would discuss with the Attorney General to scrutinise and detail the proposal in a future Act. Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji (Jelutong) supported the protection given to women and raised the right of Muslim workers to wear hijab and tudung, asking whether the government would issue a notice seeking an explanation from the Indian High Commission or any of its officials.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim opened by saying the debate concerned amendments to Acts to protect workers after the COVID-19 pandemic, and Tuan Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji [Jelutong] repeatedly asked for the Deputy Minister's position on whether children should be barred from wearing the hijab, citing India and Karnataka. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim said that wearing a tudung and covering the aurat are different matters, and said he did not wish to address the India issue. Tuan Sanisvara Nethaji Rayer a/l Rajaji [Jelutong] then asked about the government's position on the Johor Bahru situation and PAS's position, while Dato' Ramli bin Dato' Mohd Nor [Cameron Highlands] asked members to keep to the Act under discussion. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim then said the provisions on forced labour complement existing laws, naming the Private Employment Agencies Act 1981, the Passport Act 1966, the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 and the Penal Code, and that a proposal for discussions with the United States had been noted. He also addressed flexible working arrangements, sexual harassment, iddah leave for widows, and gig workers, stating that the Employment Act 1955 covers workers under a service contract and that the Ministry is studying a specific law for gig workers. Finally, he described the MYFutureJobs portal launched by PERKESO's Employment Insurance System to help employment and attract local workers to the 3D sector.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Dato' Ramli bin Dato' Mohd Nor (Cameron Highlands) presided over the second reading and committee stage of the RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021. Tuan M. Kulasegaran (Ipoh Barat) asked whether the government would carry out its earlier promise to make regulations protecting gig workers after the bill was passed, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim replied that the amendments focus on B40 groups including gig workers, that further details still need to be settled, and that the Ministry of Human Resources is studying a separate law for gig workers. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim then described the MYFutureJobs portal, which is free for job seekers and employers, and the programmes under the Sistem Insurans Pekerjaan (SIP), after Dato' Ramli asked him to wind up and then to give a written answer because time was up. Tuan Charles Anthony Santiago (Klang) sought to make an important clarification, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim said he could not be given more time and would answer in writing the points not covered in his speech. The second reading was put and agreed. In committee, Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim moved to extend maternity leave in Clause 12 from 90 to 98 days in line with ILO Convention No. 183, and Tuan M. Kulasegaran urged attention to other ILO recommendations while welcoming the extension; Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim agreed with him, and the amendment was put and agreed, with Clauses 1 to 12 then ordered to form part of the bill.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: Sivarasa Rasiah (Sungai Buloh) asked the Deputy Minister whether he would agree to an amendment without notice to change the weekly working hours in clause 20 from 45 to 40, in line with ILO standards, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim replied that 45 hours had been finalised as the amendment for today. Teo Nie Ching (Kulai) asked how the Ministry of Human Resources would ensure women are not asked about their pregnancy at job interviews, saying the protection on termination of pregnant employees in clause 13 was insufficient, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim replied that the amendment covers those already in employment and that complaints can be made to the Labour Department and through the Working For Workers portal. Karupaiya a/l Mutusami (Padang Serai) asked whether maternity leave could start two weeks before birth because of traffic in Kuala Lumpur, and Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim said the amendment raised leave from 60 to 90 days and, with the ILO annexure, to 98 days, and suggested Padang Serai discuss the matter with employers. Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim then proposed extending paternity leave in clause 23 from three days to seven days, and the amendment was agreed. M. Kulasegaran (Ipoh Barat) raised clause 30 on discrimination in employment, explaining that the bill was introduced instead of a proposed Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and asked the Deputy Minister to convey views to the Director General, Mohd Asri.

timeline.business: RANG UNDANG-UNDANG KERJA (PINDAAN) 2021 Bacaan Kali Yang Kedua dan Ketiga
timeline.summary_en: The Chairman asked the Minister to respond. Deputy Minister of Human Resources Datuk Haji Awang bin Hashim thanked the Ipoh Barat Member for raising the matter and said the clause on employment discrimination was being discussed in detail with legal parties, and that the Act may be amended again in future to better protect workers. He added that the employers' side must also be considered and agreement reached. Clauses 24 to 46 were ordered to form part of the Bill, which was reported with amendments, read a third time, supported by Deputy Minister of Industries, Plantation and Commodities II Datuk Willie anak Mongin, and passed.

answer.question: What has the government said about targeted diesel subsidies?
answer.answer:
The government has described targeted diesel subsidies in several sittings:

- **March 2024 (Deputy Finance Minister Lim Hui Ying):** Targeted subsidies would be implemented in stages, subject to readiness based on a suitable model and feasibility.[1] Diesel would be the first focus, as announced in Budget 2024.[1]
- **June 2024 (Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan):** The government said the most efficient way to curb leakage was to narrow the price gap between local diesel and global market prices.[2] Retail diesel in Peninsular Malaysia was reset to RM3.35 a litre from 10 June 2024, while prices in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan stayed at RM2.15.[2] He also projected that the government could achieve annual savings of RM4 billion.[3]
- **November 2024 (Amir Hamzah):** Diesel sales to petrol stations fell by about 25 per cent, which he said reflected reduced smuggling.[4] Based on early data, the subsidy targeting had saved about RM600 million a month.[4]
- **November 2025 (Lim Hui Ying):** The government said it was moving from bulk subsidies to targeted subsidies to optimise public spending.[5]
- **June 2026 (Amir Hamzah):** Under the announced reform, diesel would have a uniform pump price nationwide at the unsubsidised level.[6] Subsidised diesel would fall to RM2.10 a litre for eligible people, with MyKad used to verify eligibility.[6] He said the reform was expected to save RM2 billion a year in subsidy spending.[6]

This is general information from the published record, not legal advice.

passages.header: Dewan Rakyat, 2024-11-05, Parliament 15. WAKTU PERTANYAAN-PERTANYAAN MENTERI. Speakers: Menteri Kewangan (II) [Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan]; Tuan Haji Aminolhuda bin Hassan [Sri Gading] (AMANAH).
passages.text:
Tuan Haji Aminolhuda bin Hassan [Sri Gading]: minta Menteri Kewangan
menyatakan, setakat mana keberkesanan pelaksanaan penyasaran semula subsidi diesel
yang diusahakan melalui MyBUDI dan bagaimana golongan T15 ditentukan khususnya
untuk penyasaran subsidi petrol RON95 bermula pertengahan tahun 2025?

Timbalan Yang di-Pertua [Puan Alice Lau Kiong Yieng]: Silakan.

Menteri Kewangan (II) [Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan]: Terima kasih Yang
Berhormat Sri Gading atas soalan tersebut. Puan Yang di-Pertua, pada 10 Jun 2024,
kerajaan telah mengumumkan pelaksanaan penyasaran subsidi diesel yang melibatkan
kenaikan harga pam diesel di stesen minyak Semenanjung Malaysia pada harga tanpa
subsidi iaitu RM3.35 seliter, tetapi pada masa yang sama, bagi memastikan majoriti rakyat
tidak terjejas, diperkenalkan bantuan tunai untuk pemilik kenderaan individu diesel dan
petani berskala kecil serta diperkenalkan subsidi khusus untuk sektor logistik. Subsidi sektor pengangkutan barangan darat melibatkan 23 jenis kenderaan
diesel pengangkutan barangan darat di bawah Sistem Kawalan Diesel Bersubsidi (SKDS
2.0) dengan menggunakan kaedah fleet card. Sektor pengangkutan awam dan lain-lain
masih dikekalkan masing-masing pada kadar RM1.88 seliter dan RM1.65 seliter dan
pengangkutan barangan darat kekal membeli diesel pada harga subsidi RM2.15 seliter
iaitu harga pam sebelum 10 Jun 2024. Bantuan tunai BUDI MADANI sebanyak RM200
sebulan atau RM2,400 setahun disediakan untuk golongan petani, pekebun kecil serta
pemilik persendirian kenderaan diesel berdasarkan kelayakan yang ditetapkan. Untuk makluman Yang Berhormat, setakat 31 Oktober 2024, lebih 140,000
penerima BUDI Individu dan 65,000 penerima BUDI Agri-Komoditi telah diluluskan dalam
tempoh lima bulan pelaksanaan sejak Jun 2024 dengan jumlah bayaran sebanyak RM160
juta. Perlaksanaan penyasaran subsidi diesel menunjukkan penurunan mendadak dan
dari segi penjualan diesel kepada stesen minyak iaitu sekitar 25 peratus atau hampir tujuh
juta liter sehari, mencerminkan pengurangan aktiviti penyeludupan. Manakala, jualan
diesel secara komersial pula menunjukkan peningkatan hampir 50 peratus atau empat
juta liter sehari, menggambarkan setakat mana sektor industri berhenti membeli diesel
bersubsidi daripada stesen minyak. Berdasarkan data awal, penyasaran subsidi diesel setakat ini telah menjana
penjimatan sekitar RM600 juta sebulan.

passages.header: Dewan Rakyat, 2024-06-24, Parliament 15. PENERANGAN DARIPADA MENTERI KEWANGAN DI BAWAH P.M. 14(1)(i) PENYASARAN SEMULA SUBSIDI DIESEL. Speakers: Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
passages.text:
Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan (continued): Setakat 20 Jun 2024,
sebanyak 2,100 premis telah diperiksa di seluruh negara. Dan antara jumlah tersebut,
210 notis bertulis di bawah seksyen 21 Akta Kawalan Harga dan Antipencatutan 2011
telah dikeluarkan kepada peniaga di seluruh negara. Sehingga kini, sebanyak tujuh kes telah dikenal pasti hasil pelaksanaan Ops
Kesan 2.0. Analisis pencatuan akan disediakan bagi tujuan mengesan sekiranya wujud
sebarang elemen pencatut terhadap notis-notis. Selanjutnya, bermula 20 Januari 2024 juga, para pegawai penguat kuasa KPDN
di negeri Perlis, Kedah, Perak dan Kelantan telah menjalankan pemeriksaan di lapan pintu
masuk Kompleks Imigresen, Kastam, Kuarantin dan Keselamatan (ICQS) bagi
memastikan pematuhan ke atas akta dan perundangan subsidiari yang berkuat kuasa. Hampir 30,000 pemeriksaan telah dijalankan dan telah mula dikenal pasti kes yang
melibatkan kesalahan di bawah Akta Kawalan Bekalan 1961 kerana disyaki dan cuba
membawa keluar barang kawalan bersubsidi ke negara jiran. Dengan pelaksanaan
penyasaran semula subsidi diesel, diunjurkan bahawa kerajaan mampu meraih
penjimatan tahunan sebanyak RM4 bilion. Penjimatan ini tentunya dapat di manfaat untuk menambah baik mutu hidup rakyat
melalui menyediakan infrastruktur awam berkualiti serta perlindungan sosial yang lebih
menyeluruh. Perlu kita juga ditekankan bahawa berbanding dengan kos subsidi diesel
RM14 bilion tahun 2023, penjimatan RM4 bilion setahun bermakna kerajaan masih
menanggung subsidi diesel sebanyak RM10 bilion. Antaranya untuk menampung subsidi
di Sabah, Sarawak, subsidi untuk pengangkutan awam dan sektor logistik Semenanjung,
bantuan tunai untuk pemilik kenderaan individu dan pengusaha kecil agrokomoditi serta
subsidi diesel nelayan. Maknanya, walaupun kerajaan telah mengambil langkah menyasarkan subsidi
bagi mengurangkan ketirisan dan penyeludupan tetapi golongan yang memerlukan akan
terus menerima bantuan dan subsidi diesel. Pendekatan penyasaran semula subsidi
diesel yang diambil iaitu menyediakan diesel bersubsidi kepada sektor logistik dan
bantuan tunai bulanan kepada individu akan mengurangkan tekanan ke atas harga barang
pengguna dan impak kepada rakyat. Dengan itu, walaupun terdapat perubahan harga
runcit diesel yang ketara, namun dijangka tidak akan menjejaskan prestasi ekonomi atau
menjejaskan kadar inflasi. Kerajaan yakin bahawa dengan pelaksanaan penyasaran
semula subsidi diesel, ekonomi negara masih tetap mencapai unjuran rasmi kerajaan
terhadap kadar inflasi 2024 iaitu antara dua hingga 3.5 peratus serta kadar pertumbuhan
KDNK 2024 antara empat hingga lima peratus. Tan Sri Yang di-Pertua, keputusan melaksanakan penyasaran semula subsidi
diesel bukanlah satu langkah yang mudah diambil. Kerajaan tidak terburu-buru, malah
sentiasa memberi perhatian khusus untuk memastikan mekanisme terbaik digunakan
untuk melindungi sektor perniagaan dan rakyat yang layak dibantu. Keputusan ini juga
melibatkan kerjasama utuh semua pihak, sama ada jabatan kerajaan di bawah
kementerian Kewangan, Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup,
Kementerian Perladangan dan Komoditi, Kementerian Pertanian dan Keterjaminan
Makanan, Kementerian Pengangkutan mahupun syarikat minyak dan pemain industri.

passages.text:
Menteri Kewangan II [Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan] (continued): Justeru, kerajaan melanjutkan pelaksanaan BUDI MADANI kepada diesel. Seperti mana Ahli Yang Berhormat sedia maklum, konflik Asia Barat telah
melonjakkan harga minyak mentah dunia, melepasi USD120 setong dan Malaysia
tidak terkecuali daripada tempias krisis ini. Subsidi petrol dan diesel sekitar RM800
juta pada bulan Januari dan Februari sebulan telah melonjak hampir RM5 bilion
sebulan untuk Mac dan April. Walaupun terdapat petanda positif ke arah persetujuan perdamaian antara
Amerika Syarikat dan Iran, harga minyak dunia dijangka kekal tinggi berbanding
sebelum konflik bermula. Selain bekalan fiskal yang bertambah, hal yang lebih
penting ialah kelangsungan bekalan bahan api negara. Walaupun kerajaan bersama PETRONAS bertungkus-lumus
mempelbagaikan sumber bekalan bagi memastikan kelangsungan bekalan bahan
api negara, akan tetapi, usaha ini akan sia-sia sekiranya isu ketirisan tidak ditangani
dengan tegas. Hal ini lebih ketara di Sabah dan Sarawak kerana bukan warganegara
juga menikmati harga diesel bersubsidi RM2.15. Jurang harga yang besar dengan negara jiran mewujudkan ruang
penyeludupan yang sukar dibendung walaupun penguatkuasaan telah ditingkatkan. Sebagai petunjuk jelas, jumlah diesel yang terjual di stesen minyak di Sabah,
Sarawak pada bulan Mac dan April 2026 telah mencecah 200 juta liter sebulan. Ia dianggarkan dua kali ganda lebih tinggi berbanding tahap yang sepatutnya
berdasarkan bilangan kenderaan diesel yang berdaftar. Penetapan harga runcit pada
tahap tanpa subsidi di seluruh negara akan membantu menutup ketirisan ini. Oleh itu, sepertimana yang diumumkan oleh Yang Amat Berhormat Perdana
Menteri pada 21 Jun lalu, pembaharuan penyasaran subsidi diesel dilaksanakan
meliputi pertama, harga diesel di pam yang seragam iaitu harga tanpa subsidi di
seluruh negara. Kedua, cara tunggal bagi mengurus subsidi bahan api iaitu rakyat
memanfaatkan subsidi RON95 dan diesel melalui MyKad sebagai kaedah
pengesahan kelayakan dan ketiga, harga diesel bersubsidi turun kepada RM2.10
seliter untuk dinikmati rakyat yang layak. Pembaharuan BUDI MADANI membawa dua impak utama. Pertama,
kelangsungan bekalan diesel terjamin di pasaran negara dan rakyat terus menikmati
diesel pada harga yang lebih rendah. Ketirisan akibat penyeludupan dan
penyalahgunaan oleh bukan warganegara dan industri dapat dibendung dengan
lebih berkesan apabila harga di pam ditetapkan pada harga pasaran, sekali gus
menjaminkan kelangsungan bekalan di dalam pasaran negara. Malah, pembaharuan ini dijangka menjimatkan perbelanjaan subsidi
sebanyak RM2 bilion setahun yang memberi peluang kepada kerajaan untuk
mengagihkan sebahagian penjimatan untuk menurunkan harga diesel bersubsidi
kepada RM2.10 berbanding RM2.15 seliter. Bermakna, pembaharuan ini
membolehkan rakyat Malaysia mendapat keistimewaan sebagai warganegara
dengan menikmati diesel pada harga lebih rendah. Mengenai kelayakan BUDI MADANI sebanyak 200 liter, berdasarkan data
penggunaan sebenar BUDI95 sejak kita mula pada bulan Oktober 2025 sehingga
bulan Mei 2026, hanya kurang daripada satu peratus pengguna BUDI95
menggunakan lebih daripada 200 liter RON95 secara konsisten. Ini bermakna tiap-tiap bulan, dia menggunakan lebih tapi dia kurang pada satu peratus.

ketersediaan berasaskan kepada model yang bersesuaian dan kebolehlaksanaan serta
mengekalkan fokus kerajaan dalam memastikan kos sara hidup rakyat tidak terjejas. Sebagaimana yang telah diumumkan dalam Belanjawan 2024, kerajaan akan
menumpukan kepada penyasaran subsidi diesel terlebih dahulu melalui kaedah dan
mechanism yang telah diumumkan oleh Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan
Sara Hidup pada 6 Mac 2024. Perluasan pemberian di bawah Sistem Kawalan Subsidi Diesel 2.0 (SKDS 2.0)
kepada sembilan jenis kenderaan barangan telah dibuka untuk permohonan bermula 7
Mac 2024 dan dijangka memanfaatkan lebih 260,000 kenderaan. Sejak 8 Mac sehingga
16 Mac, sejumlah lebih 5,800 buah syarikat dengan lebih 34,400 bilangan kenderaan telah
berjaya mendaftar dalam SKDS 2.0. Justeru, kerajaan menyeru agar semua pemilik
kenderaan yang layak, berdaftar di bawah SKDS 2.0 agar dapat terus menikmati subsidi
di masa hadapan. Jumlah perbelanjaan subsidi diesel pada tahun 2023 telah mencecah RM14.3
bilion di mana jumlah penggunaan telah meningkat kepada 10.8 bilion liter setahun
berbanding dengan 6.1 bilion liter pada tahun 2019, sebelum pandemik COVID-19. Peningkatan jumlah penggunaan sebanyak 70 peratus ini dilihat tidak selari dengan
pertambahan bilangan kenderaan diesel yang hanya mencatatkan peningkatan kurang
dari tiga peratus. Ini mengukuhkan lagi dakwaan bahawa ketirisan subsidi diesel adalah
sangat besar. Ketika ini, semua kenderaan diesel dalam kategori pengangkutan awam di bawah
SKDS sedia ada termasuk van, bas sekolah telah menikmati harga diesel bersubsidi pada
kadar RM1.88 seliter, manakala golongan nelayan menerima subsidi diesel pada harga
RM1.65 seliter. Kedua-dua kategori ini akan kekal menikmati harga diesel tersebut dan
tidak akan terlibat dalam program pemberian subsidi diesel secara bersasar. Di samping itu, satu lagi strategi penting yang diberikan penekanan ialah
penguatkuasaan yang merupakan elemen terpenting dalam memastikan para peniaga
tidak menaikkan harga barangan dan perkhidmatan sewenang-wenangnya. Pelbagai Ops
dilaksanakan oleh Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup seperti
Ops Kesan, Ops Catut, Ops Terjah, Ops Tiris, Ops Menu, Ops Pasar dan Ops Samar bagi
memastikan bekalan sentiasa stabil dan mengekang elemen pencatutan di pasaran. Sekian, terima kasih.

Tuan Yang di-Pertua: Sandakan.

Puan Vivian Wong Shir Yee [Sandakan]: Terima kasih Timbalan Menteri atas
jawapan yang sangat menyeluruh. Soalan Sandakan adalah— Terlebih dahulu kami ingin
terima kasih kerana Sabah masih dapat enjoy subsidi diesel di Sabah, tetapi soalan saya
adalah bagaimana kementerian memastikan Sabah tidak akan menjadi salah satu tempat
penyeludupan diesel yang tertinggi sekiranya kami punya diesel punya price ada
difference di seluruh negara? Terima kasih.

Tuan Yang di-Pertua: Sila Menteri.

Puan Lim Hui Ying: Terima kasih Tan Sri Yang di-Pertua, terima kasih Yang
Berhormat Sandakan. Untuk maklumat Ahli Yang Berhormat, kerajaan melalui
Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) sentiasa komited
dalam melaksanakan kawalan berterusan ke atas penjualan dan pengedaran barang
kawalan bersubsidi bagi membendung penyelewengan dan memastikan bekalannya
sampai dan dapat dinikmati oleh rakyat negara ini.

passages.header: Dewan Rakyat, 2025-11-03, Parliament 15. PERTANYAAN-PERTANYAAN BAGI JAWAB LISAN. Speakers: Timbalan Menteri Kewangan [Puan Lim Hui Ying] (DAP); Dr. Hajah Halimah Ali [Kapar] (PAS).
passages.text:
Dr. Hajah Halimah Ali [Kapar]: minta Menteri Kewangan menyatakan, adakah
kerajaan bercadang mengawal perbelanjaan tidak produktif termasuk projek mega yang
membebankan dan menilai semula keberkesanan subsidi yang tidak sampai kepada
golongan sasaran.

Timbalan Menteri Kewangan [Puan Lim Hui Ying]: Terima kasih kepada Tuan
Yang di-Pertua. Untuk maklumat Yang Berhormat, projek-projek pembangunan masih perlu
diteruskan bagi menjana pertumbuhan ekonomi negara di samping memenuhi keperluan
rakyat. Melalui Akta Kewangan Awam dan Tanggungjawab Fiskal 2023 [Akta 850],
kerajaan mengamalkan perbelanjaan secara berhemat dan berdisiplin mengambil kira
ketetapan akta ini untuk mencapai sasaran defisit fiskal tidak melebihi tiga peratus kepada
keluaran dalam negeri kasar (KDNK), paras hutang kepada KDNK tidak melebihi 60
peratus, jaminan kerajaan kepada KDNK tidak melebihi 25 peratus dan perbelanjaan
pembangunan tahunan sekurang-kurangnya tiga peratus daripada KDNK. Sebagaimana objektif di dalam Akta 850, kerajaan sentiasa memperkukuh
kedudukan fiskal dengan mengoptimumkan perbelanjaan awam, antara lain peralihan
daripada pemberian subsidi secara pukal kepada pemberian subsidi secara bersasar. Ini
bagi memastikan subsidi dimanfaatkan oleh kumpulan yang benar-benar layak dan juga
bertujuan mengurangkan ketirisan akibat penyeludupan, sekali gus membolehkan
peruntukan yang dijimatkan disalurkan kepada program dan projek pembangunan yang
memberi manfaat langsung kepada rakyat. Kerajaan telah melaksanakan penyasaran semula subsidi seperti penyasaran
subsidi elektrik, penyasaran subsidi diesel dan penyasaran subsidi RON95. Melalui
penyasaran subsidi elektrik dan penstrukturan tarif elektrik, 85 peratus rakyat masih kekal
menikmati subsidi elektrik yang melibatkan pengguna elektrik kurang 600 kilowatt/jam dan
ada yang menikmati penurunan bil. Melalui penyasaran subsidi diesel di bawah BUDI MySubsidi Diesel pula, kerajaan
telah meluluskan kemudahan penggunaan fleet card kepada 121,618 buah syarikat yang
melibatkan 355,074 buah kenderaan. Ini masih membolehkan kenderaan tersebut
mendapatkan bekalan diesel pada harga subsidi iaitu RM2.15 seliter. Langkah ini dapat
memastikan kos operasi sektor logistik tidak meningkat secara mendadak dan barangan
keperluan kekal pada harga berpatutan. Dalam menyasarkan subsidi kepada golongan petani dan pekebun kecil serta
pemilik kenderaan diesel persendirian dan kenderaan pengangkutan darat yang layak,
kerajaan menyediakan bantuan tunai sebanyak RM200 sebulan atau RM2,400 setahun. Seramai 140,000 orang penerima yang mempunyai kenderaan diesel
persendirian aktif berdaftar di JPJ dan pendapatan tahunan individu dan pasangan tidak
melebihi RM100,000 telah menerima manfaat ini di bawah BUDI Individu. Manakala
seramai 180,000 orang golongan petani kecil dan pekebun kecil berdaftar yang menjana
nilai jualan hasil pertanian tahunan dari RM50,000 hingga RM300,000 turut menerima
manfaat yang sama di bawah BUDI Agri-Komoditi. Selain itu, bagi memastikan subsidi RON95 diberikan secara bersasar, kerajaan
telah melaksanakan inisiatif BUDI MADANI RON95 atau BUDI95 kepada seluruh rakyat
Malaysia mulai 30 September 2025.

passages.header: Dewan Rakyat, 2024-12-02, Parliament 15. PERTANYAAN-PERTANYAAN BAGI JAWAB LISAN. Speakers: Timbalan Menteri Kewangan [Puan Lim Hui Ying] (DAP); Tuan Haji Muhammad Fawwaz bin Mohamad Jan [Permatang Pauh] (PAS).
passages.text:
Tuan Haji Muhammad Fawwaz bin Mohamad Jan [Permatang Pauh]: minta
Menteri Kewangan menyatakan berapa penjimatan kerajaan daripada subsidi diesel yang
telah ditarik dan bagaimana kaedah kerajaan untuk menggunakan jumlah penjimatan ini.

Timbalan Menteri Kewangan [Puan Lim Hui Ying]: Terima kasih Tuan Yang di-Pertua, terima kasih Yang Berhormat. Untuk makluman Ahli Yang Berhormat, pada 10 Jun
2024, kerajaan telah melaksanakan penyasaran semula subsidi diesel bermula di
Semenanjung Malaysia melalui Program BUDI MADANI. Di bawah Program BUDI
MADANI, terdapat tiga subprogram utama iaitu Program MySubsidi Diesel melalui Sistem
Kawalan Diesel Bersubsidi (SKDS) 2.0, BUDI Individu dan BUDI Agri-Komoditi. Di bawah SKDS 2.0, 23 jenis kenderaan diesel pengangkutan barangan darat
yang menggunakan fleet card, kaedah fleet card akan kekal menikmati harga diesel pada
kadar RM2.15 seliter. Selain itu, kerajaan juga menyediakan bantuan tunai sebanyak
RM200 sebulan atau RM2,400 setahun kepada individu pemilik kenderaan diesel
persendirian, golongan petani dan pekebun kecil di bawah BUDI Individu dan BUDI Agri-Komoditi tertakluk kepada kriteria kelayakan yang ditetapkan. Sehingga 31 Oktober 2024,
lebih 140,000 penerima BUDI Individu dan 65,000 penerima BUDI Agri-Komoditi telah
diluluskan dalam tempoh lima bulan pelaksanaan sejak Jun 2024 dengan jumlah bayaran
sebanyak RM160 juta. Selaras dengan penyasaran semula subsidi diesel, kerajaan telah mengapungkan
harga diesel tanpa subsidi di pam bagi minggu pertama bermula 10 Jun 2024 kepada
RM3.35 sen seliter berbanding RM2.15 sen seliter melalui kaedah apungan harga secara
terkawal. Sehingga kini, kerajaan telah menurunkan harga diesel tanpa subsidi sebanyak
40 sen seliter menjadikan harga apungan semasa kini pada kadar RM2.95 sen seliter. Berdasarkan data awal, penyasaran subsidi diesel setakat ini menjana penjimatan
sekitar RM600 juta sebulan. Penjimatan yang diperoleh kerajaan daripada langkah
penting ini akan memastikan terdapat lebih banyak sumber untuk disalurkan ke dalam
sektor critical line yang secara langsung akan meningkatkan kualiti hidup rakyat termasuk
infrastruktur awam, penjagaan kesihatan dan pendidikan antaranya seperti jalan hospital
dan sekolah.
